action: Check HaveIBeenPwned and act on any notification about stolen credentials or infected machines. WordPress owners: change credentials, enable multi-factor authentication and patch. Disable Windows Script Host where it is not needed.
exec: A major disruption of criminal malware services; recovered stolen logins may lead to notifications to affected organisations.
plain: Police from nine countries took over 235 servers and 257 web addresses used to run three kinds of malicious software, and found 6.4 million sets of stolen victim data on them.

key_findings: Law enforcement and private partners actioned 235 servers and 257 domains used by Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC.
Gootloader spread through fake legal documents on hacked WordPress sites: 14 servers and 218 domains taken down, 681 infected websites remediated.
CastleRAT, a remote access trojan linked to ransomware attacks: 120 servers and 39 domains seized. StealC: 102 servers dismantled.
Over 6 million stolen victim credentials were found on the criminals' infrastructure and will be shared through HaveIBeenPwned, Shadowserver, DIVD and others.
The US Justice Department release adds that Gootloader infected at least 25,000 computers and is tied to at least 44 US ransomware victims.
report.publisher: Europol, with Eurojust and partners in nine countries
recommendations: WordPress users should update credentials, enable multi-factor authentication and patch vulnerabilities.
Check the victim-notification services named by Europol, such as HaveIBeenPwned, for stolen credentials.

summary: Europol and partners dismantled infrastructure behind the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware, seizing or disabling 235 servers and 257 domains and remediating 681 infected websites. Europol's headline counts 6.4 million victim datasets secured, to be shared through HaveIBeenPwned, Shadowserver and other services. The US Justice Department says Gootloader alone infected at least 25,000 computers.
title: Operation Endgame seizes Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC infrastructure

validation.note: Reviewed against the full original Europol release (read in a browser) and the US Department of Justice release.

review.note: Europol headline, DOJ release: 235/257, 681 sites, 25,000 computers match; plain said 6.4M passwords but Europol says victim datasets; reworded, correction filed
